help.tips[0].check.whyEn: The last part is der Trog, so the whole word is der Futtertrog.
help.tips[0].en.text: Melken + Schemel: der Schemel, so der Melkschemel. Scheune + Tor: das Tor, so das Scheunentor. Wagen + Rad: das Rad, so das Wagenrad. The first part only says what kind; the last part brings the article.
help.tips[0].en.title: Compounds follow their last part
help.tips[1].check.whyEn: Young animals are neuter: das Ferkel, das Kalb, das Fohlen.
help.tips[1].en.text: Baby animals are neuter, whatever the gender of the grown animal: das Ferkel next to die Sau, das Kalb next to die Kuh. The grown animals in this yard are not: die Ziege, die Gans, die Katze.
help.tips[1].en.title: Young animals are das
help.tips[2].check.whyEn: Nouns ending in -e are usually feminine: die Raufe, die Egge, die Sense.
help.tips[2].en.text: Many of the hand tools here end in -e, and nouns in -e are usually feminine: die Sense, die Egge, die Raufe, die Laterne, die Pumpe. Picture them in a row along the barn wall, all wearing red labels.
help.tips[2].en.title: Farm tools in -e are mostly die
help.hookEn: An old farmyard full of tools, harness and animals: tap each one in the picture, then give it its article.
help.introEn: A picture hunt instead of a deck: one cluttered farmyard in front of a red barn, with 32 things to find, many of them old rural words you meet in novels and museums rather than in daily talk — der Dreschflegel, das Kummet, die Egge, der Taubenschlag on its pole. The prompt asks Wo ist die Sense? and you tap it in the picture. Each find shows its label, coloured by its gender, then leaves a small tick in that colour, so you can see what you have already found. Once you have passed a run, the hunt turns harder: the prompt hides the article (Wo ist ___ Sense?), and after the find you choose der, die or das yourself. A tap on empty sky or grass costs nothing; a tap on the wrong object tells you what you hit and you keep looking, and after three misses the right one is shown. No object is asked twice in the same run.
help.rememberEn[0]: The last part of a compound sets the article: die Scheune + das Tor → das Scheunentor.
help.rememberEn[1]: Young animals are das: das Ferkel, das Kalb.
help.rememberEn[2]: Das Heu has no plural; one bale of it is der Heuballen.
